failures.title: IIF null expressions

removed_material.etl/informatica/README.md:
# Emulated PowerCenter estate

PowerCenter 10.5 repository exports for the `sfx-d1110` warehouse plus a Python Integration Service
(`runner/`) that runs them against the emulated Teradata warehouse (PostgreSQL).

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `repository/<FOLDER>/mappings/*.XML` | 20 Designer mapping exports (SOURCE, TARGET, TRANSFORMATION, MAPPING, CONNECTOR) |
| `repository/<FOLDER>/wf_*.XML` | Workflow Manager exports with dependencies, one workflow per file: sources, targets, mappings, sessions, worklet and workflow (`wf_SFX_BILLING_DAILY`, `wf_SFX_CONTENT_DAILY`, `wf_SFX_AUDIT_DAILY`) |
| `params/sfx_d1110_daily.par` | parameter file (`$$` mapping parameters, `$DBConnection_*` connection variables) |
| `config/connections.yaml` | relational connection `TD_SFX_EDW`, resolved from `TD_HOST TD_PORT TD_DB TD_USER TD_PASSWORD` |
| `logs/REP_SESS_LOG.psv`, `logs/REP_WFLOW_RUN.psv` | repository run history export (session and workflow runs) |
| `licence.yaml` | licence terms and the mapping-to-feature dependency list |
| `runner/` | the Integration Service and `pmcmd`-style CLI |
| `tests/fixture/` | local fixture: schema (`bootstrap.sql`) and landing files for business date 20261109 |

Folders: `SFX_BILLING` (billing and general ledger), `SFX_CONTENT` (users and documents), `SFX_AUDIT` (audit).

## Run it

```sh
make sfx-informatica-up   NS=sfx-d1110-before   # venv + warehouse database (fixture schema)
make sfx-informatica-run  NS=sfx-d1110-before   # runs the three daily workflows (MAPPINGS=20, i.e. all)
make sfx-informatica-test NS=sfx-d1110-before   # unit + integration tests
make sfx-informatica-down NS=sfx-d1110-before
```

- `INFA_DB=teradata` runs against the Teradata emulation's compose service (`make sfx-teradata-up`) instead of the
  local fixture database. The fixture database listens on `127.0.0.1:55500 + crc32(NS) % 1000`; the Teradata service on
  `54500 + crc32(NS) % 1000`.
- `MAPPINGS` selects what `sfx-informatica-run` executes: `all` or a count `N` (the first N mappings in
  `listobjects` order; 20 or more means all), or comma-separated mapping names or globs, e.g.
  `MAPPINGS=m_SFX_GL_JOURNAL_LINE` or `MAPPINGS='m_SFX_*INVOICE*,m_SFX_PAYMENT'`. Sessions of unselected mappings are
  logged as skipped and their links still fire; a workflow with no selected mapping is not started, and one whose selected
  mappings are all on disabled sessions is not started and exits with an error. `INFA_WORKFLOWS`
  narrows the workflow list (`FOLDER:workflow ...`). The runner reads the same selection from `-mappings` or `$MAPPINGS`.
- Against the seeded warehouse: `make sfx-teradata-up NS=...` then
  `make sfx-informatica-run NS=... INFA_DB=teradata` (source and target columns match `warehouse/seed/columns.py`).
- `LANDING_DIR` overrides the landing zone. It defaults to `warehouse/landing` when that has been generated, else to
  `tests/fixture/landing`. Files are read from `$PMSourceFileDir/<area>/<TABLE>/$$LOAD_DATE.psv`.
- Session logs, workflow logs, reject files, sequence state and the appended `REP_SESS_LOG.psv` are written under
  `infa_shared/<NS>/` (`PMROOTDIR`).

## pmcmd

```sh
cd etl/informatica
python -m runner startworkflow -f SFX_BILLING wf_SFX_BILLING_DAILY
python -m runner startworkflow -f SFX_AUDIT -paramfile /path/override.par wf_SFX_AUDIT_DAILY
python -m runner startsession  -f SFX_BILLING -w wf_SFX_BILLING_DAILY s_m_SFX_PAYMENT
python -m runner listobjects   -f SFX_CONTENT
```

`-sv`, `-d`, `-u`, `-p` are accepted for compatibility and ignored. The exit code is 0 when the workflow succeeds.
`INFA_MAX_SESSIONS` (default 4) caps the sessions that run at the same time.

## Runner semantics

- Transformations: Source Qualifier (source filter, SQL override, sorted ports, distinct), Expression (variable
  ports, default values), Filter, Lookup (connected and `:LKP` unconnected, cached, `Use First Value` / `Use Last Value` /
  `Report Error`), Aggregator, Router (user groups plus `DEFAULT`), Update Strategy (`DD_INSERT`, `DD_UPDATE`,
  `DD_DELETE`, `DD_REJECT`, forward rejected rows) and Sequence Generator (state kept between runs).
- Expressions follow PowerCenter null handling: a NULL condition is false in `IIF`/`DECODE(TRUE, …)`/Filter/Router,
  two-argument `IIF` returns 0, empty string or NULL by type, `||` treats NULL as empty, `NVL`, `ISNULL`, `LTRIM`,
  `RTRIM`, `TO_DATE`, `ADD_TO_DATE`, `DECODE` and the usual string, date and numeric functions.
- Writers honour `Treat source rows as`, `Insert`, `Update as Update`, `Update else Insert`, `Truncate target table
  option`, `Pre SQL` and write rejected rows to `$PMBadFileDir`. CHAR values read from the database lose trailing pad
  blanks.
- Workflows run Start, Session, Worklet, Decision and Email tasks along `WORKFLOWLINK` conditions
  (`$task.Status`, `$task.TgtFailedRows`, `$decision.Condition`). Each session logs target row counts before and after the
  load; a load that only appended rows on top of existing data is flagged as `WRT_8170`.

## SnowConvert

```sh
make sfx-informatica-snowconvert NS=sfx-d1110-before [SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION=<name>]
```

Runs SnowConvert AI (`scai init -l Teradata`, `scai code add`, `scai code convert`) on the `wf_*.XML` workflow
exports, which satisfy `scai code add`'s one-workflow-per-file check. `scai` reads the Snowflake password only from
`connections.toml`. The untouched output is copied to `snowconvert/<NS>/raw-output/` (git-ignored) with
`init.log`, `add.log` and `convert.log`. Install `scai` with
`curl -fsSL https://snowconvert.snowflake.com/storage/linux/prod/cli/install.sh | sh`.

## Tests

`python -m pytest -q tests` from this directory. Integration tests create a fresh database on the server given by
`TD_*`; when none is reachable and `TD_PORT` is unset they start a throwaway `postgres:16` container.

import datetime as dt
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from runner import expr as X


def ev(text, row=None, types=None, params=None):
    return X.compile_expr(text, X.CompileContext(port_types=types or {}, params=params or {}))(row or {})


ROW = {"A": None, "B": "x", "N": 5, "D": dt.datetime(2024, 1, 31)}
TYPES = {"A": "string", "B": "string", "N": "integer", "D": "date/time"}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text,expected", [
    ("IIF(A = 'x', 'Y', 'N')", "N"),           # null condition takes the false branch
    ("IIF(A = 'x', 'Y')", ""),                 # two-argument IIF defaults to empty string for strings
    ("IIF(N > 9, N)", 0),                      # ... and to zero for numbers
    ("IIF(ISNULL(A), 'missing', A)", "missing"),
    ("NVL(A, B)", "x"),
    ("ISNULL(A)", 1),
    ("A || B", "x"),                           # null concatenates as empty
    ("LTRIM('  ab ')", "ab "),
    ("RTRIM('  ab  ')", "  ab"),
    ("LTRIM(A)", None),
    ("DECODE(B, 'x', 1, 'y', 2, 0)", 1),
    ("DECODE(A, NULL, 'null-match', 'other')", "null-match"),
    ("DECODE(TRUE, N > 9, 'a', N > 3, 'b', 'c')", "b"),
    ("A = 1 OR 1 = 1", 1),
    ("A = 1 AND 1 = 0", 0),
    ("NOT A = 1", None),
    ("N + A", None),
])
def test_null_semantics(text, expected):
    assert ev(text, ROW, TYPES) == expected


def test_dates():
    assert ev("TO_DATE('2026-11-09 10:11:12', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS')") == dt.datetime(2026, 11, 9, 10, 11, 12)
    assert ev("TO_DATE(A, 'YYYY-MM-DD')", ROW, TYPES) is None
    assert ev("ADD_TO_DATE(D, 'MM', 1)", ROW, TYPES) == dt.datetime(2024, 2, 29)

# Act 1: Assess

Offline only; no connections, credentials, or changes to the source estate.
Run from the repository root with Python 3, PyYAML and pytest installed:

```sh
python migration/dw-exit/tools/check.py # fails before generation
python migration/dw-exit/tools/assess.py
python migration/dw-exit/tools/check.py
python -m pytest migration/dw-exit/tests -q
```

The generator overwrites only the assessment outputs in this directory. Inputs
are the checked-out estate, registry, DBQL CSVs, licence YAML and planted risk
registers. Generated IDs use stable SHA-256 prefixes, lists and edges are sorted,
and no wall-clock values are used. See `plan.md` for interpretation and limits.

## Live assessment control plane

Install `requirements.txt` in a virtual environment outside the repository.
Bind SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT, SNOWFLAKE_USER, SNOWFLAKE_ROLE, SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE,
SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY and SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TOKEN from the credential store per
invocation. The PEM key is parsed only in memory, never written or printed.
Only SFX_D1110_AFTER is accepted; the warehouse is fixed to SFX_D1110_OPS_WH.
Every connection starts with the compact assess/preflight QUERY_TAG, then sets
the phase tag before executing work. Every command suspends the warehouse in
its cleanup path, including a failed verification.

```sh
python migration/dw-exit/tools/control.py verify # expected missing-schema failure before first load
python migration/dw-exit/tools/control.py load
python migration/dw-exit/tools/control.py verify
python migration/dw-exit/tools/control.py report
python migration/dw-exit/tools/control.py history
```

`load` creates six tables and four views with the run/expiry comment. DML replaces
all input datasets in one transaction, preserving table definitions. It resets
statuses: do not rerun after later-act progress without intending that reset.
MANIFEST has mutable STATUS, UPDATED_AT and UPDATED_BY_ACT fields. Later acts
must explicitly update the latter two alongside status (no automatic trigger).
The licence view counts objects still present until status becomes done/retired;
planning a retirement alone does not reduce the counter. Spark is measured zero.

The hidden-consumer SQL anti-joins SELECT principals against repository scan
hits, excluding identities also observed as ETL/UTILITY/BATCH. Thus batch accounts
missing from repository text do not become hidden end-user consumers. The dead
view independently anti-joins TablesV against all DBQL usage in the 90-day window.
`query_history_assess.sql` is the exact proof query over the last day, up to 10,000
queries, grouped by phase and execution status. No renders are committed.

# Act 2: Billing — prove before promoting

This run migrates the billing estate into `SFX_D1110_AFTER.BILLING`. It does not
depend on the target scaffold or alter another subject area's control rows.
`TD_BASELINE` is a value-exact capture of the post-daily-chain emulator, not
expected values recomputed in Snowflake. Capture uses CREATE, never REPLACE,
and checks the uploaded rows against the source as a duplicate-preserving bag.
The baseline must not be recaptured between red and green.

## Reproduce

Use the existing org key-pair credentials in the environment. Never put a key
in a command, repository file or log. All Snowflake sessions use a JSON query
tag for run `sfx-d1110`, act `prove`; only `SFX_D1110_*` warehouses are used.
All explicitly created Snowflake objects carry
`run_token=sfx-d1110 expires=2026-11-24` as their COMMENT.

```sh
make sfx-teradata-up NS=sfx-d1110-before ROWS_PER_TABLE=20000
make sfx-teradata-run NS=sfx-d1110-before BUSINESS_DATE=20261109
make warehouse/.venv/.billing-requirements
# Install SnowConvert AI per warehouse/teradata/README.md first.
warehouse/.venv/bin/python migration/dw-exit/billing/snowconvert.py
# Fresh TD_BASELINE only. Refuses to overwrite existing capture tables.
make sfx-billing-capture NS=sfx-d1110-before BUSINESS_DATE=20261109

# Expected failure. Preserve this file before proceeding.
make sfx-billing-prove CANDIDATE=initial BUSINESS_DATE=20261109
# Same BEFORE, same tests, corrected conversion.
make sfx-billing-prove CANDIDATE=fixed BUSINESS_DATE=20261109

# Supplemental probes are a separate manifest, never counted as billing.
PYTHONPATH=migration/dw-exit warehouse/.venv/bin/python -m parity.ladder \
  --manifest migration/dw-exit/parity/supplemental.json \
  --step supplemental_red --output migration/dw-exit/.runs/supplemental-initial.json
warehouse/.venv/bin/python migration/dw-exit/billing/probes.py
PYTHONPATH=migration/dw-exit warehouse/.venv/bin/python -m parity.ladder \
  --manifest migration/dw-exit/parity/supplemental.json \
  --step supplemental_green --output migration/dw-exit/.runs/supplemental-fixed.json
make sfx-billing-promote
make sfx-billing-test
```

The SnowConvert wrapper encrypts the runtime `.p8` with a random in-memory
passphrase, passed to the child through its environment. The existing connection
writer keeps the key and TOML outside the repo with mode 600. SnowConvert's
ignored conversion/report directories preserve its original output; `billing/initial`
contains the minimally executable red candidate after syntax-only repairs, not a
claim that raw converter output compiles. `billing/` contains the corrected SQL.
Never run capture or conversion unattended in CI; CI runs offline regressions only.

## Conversion map

| Source | Target |
|---|---|
| Billing DDL, staging tables | `billing/00_tables.sql` |
| Load BTEQ 01–05 | `billing/10_load.sql` |
| Incoming storage billing from documents BTEQ 10 | `billing/15_storage.sql`, from captured `STORAGE_USAGE_INPUT` |
| Subscription and currency report BTEQ 10–11, macros | Snowflake SQL table-returning procedures in `billing/20_routines.sql`; output snapshots |
| Monthly invoice BTEQ 12, stored procedure | `P_MONTHLY_INVOICE`, Snowflake Scripting with explicit transaction and SQLROWCOUNT |
| Period-close BTEQ 13, exports | `billing/40_close.sql`, `billing/reports.py` |
| Stacked views 10/20 | `billing/30_views.sql` |

The input loads and monthly calculation remain separate. Staging is loaded from
the captured raw input, not copied from final expected billing tables. The
monthly procedure calculates invoice lines, taxes, currency control totals and
balanced journal entries from those inputs. BTEQ export directives become
queryable result tables. `promote.py` rechecks every billing relation before
upserting billing-only rows in `SFX_D1110_AFTER.MIGRATION_CONTROL.OBJECTS`.
The shared assessment schema is reused; `MANIFEST` and other subjects' rows
are not modified. Staging inputs get a separate fresh parity check before
their object rows are verified. FastLoad jobs are outside this act and are
not marked verified. Missing control schema/table is bootstrapped with the
required run-token COMMENT. No PUBLIC schema or parallel register is used.
The red candidate intentionally omits the incoming storage boundary; green
includes its conversion. No final billing output is copied to make green pass.

## Parity contract

`parity/billing.json` lists only billing relations. The reusable ladder accepts
fully qualified relations and explicit keys. It runs every stage even if the
previous stage failed: counts; per-column null/min/max/distinct profiles;
SHA-256 hashes grouped by key **and multiplicity**; then exact value comparisons
for deterministic mismatch keys (or deterministic matching keys on green).
Hash differences count unmatched row occurrences on both sides; they are not
distinct business-key counts. Decimal serialization ignores declared scale, not
numeric value. Text is never trimmed or case-folded by the parity tool.
Profiles and full hashes cover all rows; value diffs are a sample, not an
exhaustive display. JSON output includes executed SQL and query IDs.

`SFX_LIVE_PARITY=1` enables the manifest-driven pytest. Without credentials, the
live cases are explicitly skipped; offline tests still prove fail-closed behavior,
padding sensitivity, SQL identifier validation and duplicate multiplicity.

Render side-by-side evidence with `python -m parity.report --red <billing-red.json>
--green <billing-fixed.json> --supplemental-red <probe-red.json>
--supplemental-green <probe-green.json> --output <report.md>`, with
`PYTHONPATH=migration/dw-exit` and the warehouse virtualenv's Python.

## Semantic ownership

Billing exercises CHAR padding, NOT CASESPECIFIC joins/grouping, FORMAT casts
and Teradata integer-date arithmetic. Conversion fixes belong in load/routine/
view SQL, never the oracle or parity tests. The date FORMAT must be explicit and
must survive a session using a different display format.

The source billing tables are MULTISET. SET suppression, truncation and QUALIFY
ties therefore live in **supplemental probes** under `BILLING_PROBES`, with a
separate unchanged baseline and manifest. The fixture explicitly chooses the
highest version ID when timestamps tie; it does not pretend tied ROW_NUMBER is
deterministic without that contract. MULTISET duplicates stay intact.

Finance decision: preserve legacy SET exact-duplicate suppression and expose
suppressed rows for review. `BILLING_PROBES.SET_ROWS` still uses full-row
DISTINCT, never business-key deduplication. The supplemental view
`SFX_D1110_AFTER.BILLING_PROBES.SET_DUPLICATE_QUARANTINE` groups the preserved
raw FEED by every payload column (ID and VALUE) and includes only repeated
rows. INPUT_COUNT counts all copies, RETAINED_COUNT is one, and
SUPPRESSED_COUNT is INPUT_COUNT minus one. Null payloads group together;
different values sharing a key remain separate. The view does not feed totals
or change any billing MULTISET rows. It reflects the retained FEED, not an
append-only history across future feed replacements.

Finance can review the exact payload and counts with:

```sql
SELECT ID, VALUE, INPUT_COUNT, RETAINED_COUNT, SUPPRESSED_COUNT
FROM SFX_D1110_AFTER.BILLING_PROBES.SET_DUPLICATE_QUARANTINE
ORDER BY ID, VALUE;
```

Run `query_history.sql` to retrieve the tagged audit trail, including failed
conversion attempts, both parity runs, promotion and control-table verification.

"""Render captured red and green ladder runs without inventing measurements."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path


def table(before, after):
    old = {row['name']: row for row in before}
    new = {row['name']: row for row in after}
    if not old or old.keys() != new.keys():
        raise ValueError('Both runs must contain the same nonempty relation set')
    lines = ['| Relation | BEFORE rows | Red rows | Green rows | Profile gaps red → green | Hash gaps red → green | Result |',
             '|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|']
    for name, red in old.items():
        green = new[name]
        if red['before_count'] != green['before_count']:
            raise ValueError(f'{name}: baseline row count changed')
        status = lambda row: 'GREEN' if row['passed'] else 'RED'
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {red['before_count']:,} | {red['after_count']:,} | {green['after_count']:,} | "
                     f"{red['profile_mismatched_columns']} → {green['profile_mismatched_columns']} | "
                     f"{red['hash_difference']:,} → {green['hash_difference']:,} | {status(red)} → {status(green)} |")
    return '\n'.join(lines)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--red', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--green', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--supplemental-red', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--supplemental-green', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    read = lambda path: json.loads(path.read_text())
    text = '# Live billing parity: red to green\n\n'
    text += table(read(args.red), read(args.green))
    text += '\n\n## Supplemental probes — not billing\n\n'
    text += table(read(args.supplemental_red), read(args.supplemental_green))
    text += ('\n\nProfiles cover null counts, min, max and distinct counts. Hash gaps are unmatched '
             'row occurrences, including duplicates; they are not distinct bad business keys. '
             'Every relation also runs sampled value-by-value checks. Raw JSON records SQL and query IDs.\n\n'
             'Finance decision: preserve legacy SET exact-duplicate suppression and expose '
             'suppressed payloads with counts in BILLING_PROBES.SET_DUPLICATE_QUARANTINE. '
             'Billing MULTISET duplicates remain preserved.\n')
    args.output.write_text(text)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
from collections import Counter
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3

import pytest

from parity.connection import COMMENT

SOURCE = (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'billing/supplemental.sql').read_text()
FEED = 'SFX_D1110_AFTER.BILLING_PROBES.FEED'
VIEW = 'SFX_D1110_AFTER.BILLING_PROBES.SET_DUPLICATE_QUARANTINE'
DEFINITION = SOURCE.split('CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ' + VIEW, 1)[1].split(';', 1)[0]
QUERY = 'SELECT ' + DEFINITION.split('AS SELECT ', 1)[1]


@pytest.mark.parametrize('rows', [[], [(1, 'x')], [(1, 'x')] * 2,
    [(1, 'x')] * 3 + [(1, 'y')] * 2 + [(2, 'x')],
    [(None, None)] * 2 + [(1, None)] * 3,
    [(1, 'x'), (1, 'X'), (1, 'x '), (1, 'x')]])
def test_exact_duplicate_payloads_and_extra_copy_counts(rows):
    with sqlite3.connect(':memory:') as db:
        db.execute('CREATE TABLE feed (id INTEGER, value TEXT)')
        db.executemany('INSERT INTO feed VALUES (?,?)', rows)
        actual = db.execute(QUERY.replace(FEED, 'feed')).fetchall()
        expected = [(*row, count, 1, count - 1)
                    for row, count in Counter(rows).items() if count > 1]
        assert Counter(actual) == Counter(expected)
        assert sum(row[-1] for row in actual) == len(rows) - len(set(rows))


def test_quarantine_does_not_change_set_or_multiset_conversion():
    assert f"COMMENT = '{COMMENT}'" in DEFINITION
    assert f'AS SELECT DISTINCT ID, VALUE FROM {FEED};' in SOURCE
    multiset = SOURCE.split('CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE SFX_D1110_AFTER.BILLING_PROBES.MULTISET_ROWS', 1)[1].split(';', 1)[0]
    assert f'AS SELECT * FROM {FEED}' in multiset
    assert 'BILLING.' not in DEFINITION

def test_live_quarantine_reconciles_exact_suppressed_rows():
    from parity.connection import connect
    with connect('set_quarantine_regression') as sf, sf.cursor() as cursor:
        cursor.execute(f'SELECT ID,VALUE FROM {FEED}')
        feed = Counter(cursor.fetchall())
        cursor.execute('SELECT ID,VALUE FROM SFX_D1110_AFTER.BILLING_PROBES.SET_ROWS')
        retained = Counter(cursor.fetchall())
        assert retained == Counter({row: 1 for row in feed})
        cursor.execute(f'SELECT ID,VALUE,INPUT_COUNT,RETAINED_COUNT,SUPPRESSED_COUNT FROM {VIEW}')
        actual = cursor.fetchall()
        assert Counter(actual) == Counter([(*row, count, 1, count - 1)
                                          for row, count in feed.items() if count > 1])
        assert sum(row[-1] for row in actual) == sum(feed.values()) - sum(retained.values())

-- m_SFX_APP_USER: STG_APP_USER -> LKP_APP_USER (target, Use First Value) -> UPD_APP_USER.
-- IIF(ISNULL(lkp_USER_ID), DD_INSERT, DD_UPDATE) is an upsert on the target key,
-- so it becomes an incremental MERGE on USER_ID. Reruns update rows in place.
{{ config(materialized='incremental', incremental_strategy='merge', unique_key='USER_ID') }}
select
    USER_ID,
    cast(left(DISPLAY_NAME, 60) as varchar(60)) as DISPLAY_NAME,
    cast(left(EMAIL, 120) as varchar(120)) as EMAIL,
    cast(left(STATUS_CD, 12) as varchar(12)) as STATUS_CD,
    CREATED_DT
from {{ ref('pc_content__stg_app_user') }}

-- m_SFX_DOC_SHARE: FF_DOC_SHARE -> EXP_DOC_SHARE -> LKP_ROLE_GRANT -> EXP_ACCESS_LEVEL -> DOC_SHARE.
-- The session treats source rows as update with update else insert, so this is a MERGE on SHARE_ID.
--
-- LKP_ROLE_GRANT reads SFX_USERS.ROLE_GRANT on USER_ID with Use First Value. That table is
-- loaded by m_SFX_ROLE_GRANT, which another effort owns, so the lookup source is rebuilt here
-- from the same landing file with the same expression: UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(ROLE_CD))) into CHAR(12).
-- The runner builds the cache with ORDER BY USER_ID and keeps load order for ties. The load
-- order is GRANT_ID order, so the first match is the lowest GRANT_ID for each user.
--
-- DECODE(TRUE, ...) treats a NULL condition as false. A user with no grant falls through to
-- ACCESS_LEVEL. CASE has the same NULL rule.
{{ config(materialized='incremental', incremental_strategy='merge', unique_key='SHARE_ID') }}
with src as (
    select
        cast(SHARE_ID as bigint) as SHARE_ID,
        cast(DOCUMENT_ID as bigint) as DOCUMENT_ID,
        cast(USER_ID as bigint) as USER_ID,
        upper(trim(ACCESS_LEVEL, ' ')) as ACCESS_LEVEL,
        cast(SHARED_DT as date) as SHARED_DT
    from {{ source('pc_content_src', 'DOC_SHARE') }}
),
role_grant as (
    select
        cast(USER_ID as bigint) as USER_ID,
        left(upper(trim(ROLE_CD, ' ')), 12) as ROLE_CD
    from {{ source('pc_content_src', 'ROLE_GRANT') }}
    qualify row_number() over (partition by cast(USER_ID as bigint) order by GRANT_ID) = 1
)
select
    s.SHARE_ID,
    s.DOCUMENT_ID,
    s.USER_ID,
    cast(left(case
        when r.ROLE_CD = 'ADMIN' then 'OWNER'
        when r.ROLE_CD = 'EDITOR' and s.ACCESS_LEVEL = 'VIEW' then 'EDIT'
        else s.ACCESS_LEVEL
    end, 12) as varchar(12)) as ACCESS_LEVEL,
    s.SHARED_DT
from src s
left join role_grant r on r.USER_ID = s.USER_ID

-- m_SFX_DOCUMENT: STG_DOCUMENT -> EXP_OWNER_CHECK (:LKP.LKP_APP_USER_STATUS(OWNER_USER_ID))
-- -> FIL_KNOWN_OWNER (NOT ISNULL(o_OWNER_STATUS)) -> LKP_DOCUMENT -> UPD_DOCUMENT.
-- The unconnected lookup reads APP_USER on USER_ID with Use First Value. The runner orders
-- the cache by USER_ID; APP_USER.USER_ID is the primary key, so the first match is the only match.
-- A NULL owner id, an unknown owner or a NULL owner status all make the filter drop the row.
-- IIF(ISNULL(lkp_DOCUMENT_ID), DD_INSERT, DD_UPDATE) becomes a MERGE on DOCUMENT_ID.
{{ config(materialized='incremental', incremental_strategy='merge', unique_key='DOCUMENT_ID', on_schema_change='append_new_columns') }}
with owner_status as (
    select USER_ID, STATUS_CD
    from {{ ref('pc_content__app_user') }}
    qualify row_number() over (partition by USER_ID order by USER_ID) = 1

select

# migrations-page evidence (UNT-2)

## UNT-3 audit mapping successor

`parity.evidence_unt3` owns only `m_SFX_STG_AUDIT_EVENT` and
`m_SFX_AUDIT_EVENT`, selected by `mappings/sfx_audit.yml`. Its read-only
`preflight` freezes full PC_SRC rows, both PC_BEFORE readbacks, control rows and
initial PC_AUDIT relation metadata. All evidence is under `out/evidence/unt3`;
each phase retains SQL/QIDs in `queries.json` and `transcript.txt`. Only `run`
invokes dbt; preflight/postflight/replay never issue writes. Do not run `run`
until exclusive target access is coordinated. No full-refresh is used.

The accepted manifest SHA256 is
`b5e0c8a390fba31c4f5f4b930d82d54102eb09e8e35837c90f1096168b67c41c`.
`oracle1` is `unt2_oracle_d53b0b939dd5`, not oracle2 (another oracle execution,
not dbt). Superseded oracle run directories are never selected. The immutable
manifest, implementation file hashes, oracle session lineage/status and full
input rows are checked, not merely row counts.

### Exact semantics and representations

- STG: canonical session truncate YES / Insert, XML lines 597/610; dbt table
  replacement. AUDIT_EVENT: XML lines 640-655 says Update else Insert YES,
  truncate NO and Update. Incremental merge on EVENT_ID updates every non-key
  column and inserts missing keys, preserving unrelated existing target rows.
  This is runner/engine.py:791-818,866-899, not truncate+insert. Initial target
  must be absent or empty; a populated initial AUDIT_EVENT stops before writes.
- Duplicate source EVENT_IDs are never deduped. Runner flushes pending inserts
  before each update (engine.py:880-899), so repeated keys are sequential
  last-write-wins, including a key initially absent. Snowflake MERGE with duplicate
  matches is not equivalent; the evidence run checks the complete STG input
  equals oracle1 and has no duplicate keys before either audit merge. Preflight
  reports duplicate counts on the frozen input and both oracle readbacks.
- String SQ coercion slices before expression evaluation
  (engine.py:26-35,339-367). EVENT_TYPE is sliced to 12 and DETAILS to 160 before
  trimming. Expression output coercion also enforces 12/160 on AUDIT_EVENT
  (engine.py:450-482). Target varchar is not itself sliced by `db_value`
  (engine.py:63-76); database types enforce target widths. No columns excluded.
- `IIF` missing else for bigint is 0, not NULL, including NULL > 0:
  expr.py:924-931,960-973 and truthy at 266-275. Thus both nonpositive/null
  DOCUMENT_ID and CUSTOMER_ID produce 0. Comparisons with NULL produce NULL,
  then the IIF condition treats it as false. `||` treats NULL as empty except
  both operands NULL (expr.py:697-700). The fallback DETAILS includes the literal
  ` by user `, even with null EVENT_TYPE/ACTOR_USER_ID. TO_CHAR(bigint) uses its
  unformatted integer string (expr.py:647-652,327-337). TRIM defaults to spaces
  only; NULL remains NULL, empty remains empty (expr.py:555-562,730-734).
- File NULL_CHARACTER `*` is ignored by the runner: the actual file reader
  makes only empty fields NULL (engine.py:369-397); a literal `*` remains a
  string. Shared PC_SRC uses bootstrap STG types and COPY with
  EMPTY_FIELD_AS_NULL TRUE / NULL_IF empty (parity/harness.py:75-108), so the
  same empty/null representation is already present. Bigints and timestamps
  are already typed; numeric/date conversion failures cannot occur on this
  frozen input. TRY_ predicates are retained in the SQL and reused verbatim by
  read-only reject exports. This is not certification of arbitrary malformed
  landing strings: runner TO_BIGINT even accepts a numeric prefix and truncates
  decimals toward zero (expr.py:618-630); typed PC_SRC cannot retain such strings.
- ERROR defaults do not substitute values: transformation failures increment
  failed source rows and drop the row (engine.py:191-199,435-482). Contrary to
  generic reject-file expectations, only writer rejects emit `.bad` records
  (engine.py:835-840); empty `.bad` files are removed (914-915). Both accepted
  oracle sessions must have zero failed source/target rows. Reject export is a
  full typed input-row multiset selected with the model's exact predicate;
  empty raw oracle `.bad` translates unambiguously to an empty typed multiset.
  Nonempty raw oracle rejects fail closed rather than inventing a lossy decoding.
  There are no Snowflake reject tables.
- Explicit NUMBER(38,0), TIMESTAMP_NTZ(0) and VARCHAR(200/160/12) casts represent
  the oracle bigint/timestamp(0)/varchar/char columns. PostgreSQL char(12) pads;
  Snowflake CHAR does not, so RPAD is representation-only, preserving all spaces.
  DESCRIBE validates actual warehouse types before metadata is mapped to oracle
  type descriptors using `evidence_live.fetched(source_loading=True)` for dbt
  outputs; PC_BEFORE uses its established TIMESTAMP_NTZ(9) storage translation.
  No decimal scale, null/empty, timestamp value or whitespace is normalized away.

### Build side effects (selection without parents or descendants)

`run_dbt.py build --select pc_audit__stg_audit_event` builds that single table
and its warning-only duplicate test. Source PC_SRC.AUDIT_EVENT is SELECT-only.
The installed dbt-snowflake 1.9.0 table materialization directly issues
CREATE OR REPLACE TRANSIENT TABLE STG_AUDIT_EVENT AS (the model SELECT), not an
intermediate/backup rename sequence. It may create the PC_AUDIT schema if absent; dbt also
issues session/query-tag and relation-cache metadata statements. No downstream
AUDIT_EVENT model is selected. Test failure SELECTs do not store rows by default.
Persist-docs and the PC post-hook comment on the built table. On-run-end
`reapply_governance(results)` writes ONLY successful built relations:
`ALTER TABLE SFX_D1110_AFTER.PC_AUDIT.STG_AUDIT_EVENT SET TAG
SFX_D1110_AFTER.GOVERNANCE.SFX_RUN = 'sfx-d1110'`, then COMMENT with the model
description. No policy attachments apply (`governance_policies: {}`).
`pc_finalize_comments(results)` rewrites ONLY that table's comment to
`run_token=sfx-d1110 expires=2026-11-24`. Tag-setting is a write on our relation,
not on other tables. No control, PC_BEFORE, RAW/CORE/MART, or other PC relations
are written. Exact adapter SQL should be retained from the tagged query history
when builds are authorized. STG has no temporary/backup relation on this adapter;
the incremental audit source view is named AUDIT_EVENT__dbt_tmp.

The incremental audit build initially creates its table if absent. Subsequent
runs create a temporary source view, DESCRIBE source/target columns, then MERGE
on EVENT_ID, updating all columns (including the unchanged key) and inserting
missing rows; the temporary view is dropped. Hooks apply only to AUDIT_EVENT.

### Commands after access coordination

From `warehouse/`, with existing in-memory JWT secret bindings:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt3 preflight
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt3 run --mapping m_SFX_STG_AUDIT_EVENT --run 1
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt3 run --mapping m_SFX_STG_AUDIT_EVENT --run 2
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt3 replay --mapping m_SFX_STG_AUDIT_EVENT
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt3 run --mapping m_SFX_AUDIT_EVENT --run 1
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt3 run --mapping m_SFX_AUDIT_EVENT --run 2
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt3 replay --mapping m_SFX_AUDIT_EVENT
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt3 postflight
```

Do not recapture preflight over existing initial-state evidence. Each `run` uses
a UUID query-tag step and preserves combined raw stdout/stderr, dbt log,
run_results adapter responses, tagged query history SQL/QIDs and UTC execution
bounds. No resets, full-refreshes or source changes between run1 and run2.

The local commands never connect to Snowflake. Live commands use the existing JWT
connector with an in-memory key and never write control rows.
HARNESS self-tests and two fresh oracle executions are **not mapping parity**.
The canonical XML and runner remain unchanged. `scope()` expands the owned config
with folder/workflow/session/targets, reject filenames, parameters, disabled-task
reasons and sequence initial values from canonical exports; the manifest records
that full resolved configuration.

## UNT-4 audit daily summary and archive

Scope: `m_SFX_AUDIT_DAILY_SUMMARY` -> `PC_AUDIT.AUDIT_DAILY_SUMMARY` and
`m_SFX_AUDIT_EVENT_ARCHIVE` -> `PC_AUDIT.AUDIT_EVENT_ARCHIVE`, built on UNT-3
(`PC_AUDIT.AUDIT_EVENT`, unchanged and re-verified row-for-row before every run).
Executed candidate b64d903a35c4af58a53f78b50fd0346a97cef8b0. `evidence_unt4.py` refuses to
run if HEAD or any implementation file hash changes after preflight.

Summary: `AGG_DAILY_EVENTS` groups by `TRUNC(EVENT_TS,'DD')` and `CUSTOMER_ID`.
`SEQ_AUDIT_SUMMARY` starts at 50001. The runner numbers groups in the order it
first sees them, which is EVENT_ID order for the audit target. Ranking the
accepted UNT-2 oracle's groups by `MIN(EVENT_ID)` reproduces all 118
SUMMARY_IDs, so the model uses that ordering. **Intended difference:** the
legacy session is Insert with no truncate, so a rerun appends 118 duplicate
groups with new IDs (`tests/test_runner_integration.py`). dbt instead MERGEs on
SUMMARY_ID. Existing groups keep their IDs (run 2 rewrites the 118 matched rows
with identical values), and new groups continue from MAX(SUMMARY_ID)+1.
First-load parity includes generated IDs. Legacy second-run equivalence is
**not** claimed.

Archive: the source filter is `EVENT_TS < CURRENT_DATE - $$ARCHIVE_DAYS`, using
the session override of 2555 days, not the workflow default of 730. The date is
the UTC date, matching the runner's PostgreSQL session (`Etc/UTC`).
`SEQ_AUDIT_ARCHIVE` starts at 1, in EVENT_ID order. The session stays
**disabled** in `wf_SFX_AUDIT_DAILY` (`ISENABLED="NO"`), and the XML, params and
oracle are unchanged. On replay, dbt appends only the occurrences of a complete
key tuple that are not archived yet, so a rerun adds nothing (**intended
difference**: a legacy rerun re-archives everything with new IDs).

The frozen archive oracle is empty, so `fixture-runner` builds two isolated,
test-only cases in throwaway local PostgreSQL databases and runs the real
`startsession` twice. The 13 source events cover:
- one second before the cutoff, exactly at it and one second after;
- a NULL timestamp;
- all-NULL columns;
- whitespace, a 160-character value, and empty-string versus NULL DETAILS;
- an event older than 730 days but newer than 2555;
- the oldest event with the latest EVENT_ID.

`empty` starts from an empty target and sequence 1. `history` starts with three
prior rows (IDs 7-9) and a persisted sequence of 10. `fixture-load` copies the
identical source and initial target into `PC_AUDIT_UNT4_FIXTURE`, which is the
only schema the guarded writes may touch, and verifies the copy against
PostgreSQL by full multiset comparison. The fixture models are enabled only with
`SFX_UNT4_ARCHIVE_FIXTURE=1` and share the production macro
`pc_audit_event_archive`. A fixture run aborts if the Snowflake UTC date differs
from the runner's CURRENT_DATE.

```sh
cd warehouse  # bind secret:org:SNOWFLAKE_* references at exec time only
TD_PORT=<local pg> .venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt4 fixture-runner --scenario empty
TD_PORT=<local pg> .venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt4 fixture-runner --scenario history
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt4 fixture-load
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt4 preflight
for s in empty history m_SFX_AUDIT_DAILY_SUMMARY m_SFX_AUDIT_EVENT_ARCHIVE; do
  .venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt4 run --subject $s --run 1
  .venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt4 run --subject $s --run 2
  .venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt4 replay --subject $s; done
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt4 postflight
```

Each replay compares typed full-row multisets (oracle vs run 1, oracle vs run 2,
and run 1 vs run 2) and business-key multiplicities. It also checks that
sequence IDs are stable, that runner sessions report SUCCEEDED, FAILED_ROWS=0
and no `.bad` rows, and that no query wrote the target between the two runs
(QUERY_HISTORY_BY_USER window). Neither dbt model has a reject path.

Not certified:
- archive key-tuple collisions (the shared gate fails them by contract);
- source orders that differ from EVENT_ID order;
- archives that are also written by other jobs, where MAX(ID)+1 differs from the
  persisted sequence;
- summary NULL EVENT_TS groups;
- Task DAG execution, control marking (UNT-10) and CI.

## Reproduce local baseline

From repository root:

```sh
make warehouse/.venv/.sfx-installed
make sfx-informatica-up NS=sfx-d1110-before
cd warehouse
.venv/bin/python -m pytest parity/tests -q
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence manifest
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence oracle
```

The namespace-scoped compose target starts only local PostgreSQL and installs the
runner environment. Each capture creates and drops its own UUID database; logs
and state survive under `parity/out/evidence/unt2_oracle_*`. No shared PC_SRC or
PC_BEFORE uploads occur. Audit runs through `startworkflow`; the three owned
content sessions run through `startsession`, not `wf_SFX_CONTENT_DAILY`, because
that canonical workflow would execute five unowned mappings. Archive runs
standalone without enabling its canonical workflow task.

`manifest.json` freezes landing hashes/counts, resolved session parameters,
bootstrap hash, initial target/source tables and sequence defaults/storage.
Oracle verifies that manifest before each execution. Retain that file unchanged.
Per mapping, `oracle1/` and `oracle2/` contain target typed JSON and typed-cell CSV,
raw reject lines as JSON and CSV, and session results. Reject lines preserve the
runner's own lossy null/empty encoding rather than inventing values. The original
`.bad` files and session/workflow logs remain in each run directory.
`oracle_determinism.json` includes complete multiset differences and reject counts.

## Successor mapping replay protocol

Coordinate exclusive access to the exact owned target. Confirm unchanged source
hashes/parameters against the manifest and record initial target/sequence state.
Execute the scoped dbt node once, capture **all** target rows and rejects, then
execute that same node again without truncation, full-refresh, restore or source
changes. Capture all rows/rejects again and retain execution logs/query IDs.
These execution requirements cannot be proven by snapshot comparison alone.

Serialize each target snapshot as `{columns, types, rows}` using `snapshot()`'s
typed-cell layout. Preserve nulls, string whitespace, numeric precision/scale and
timestamp timezone/precision. Cross-engine type translation must be explicitly
reviewed and representation-only; this strict baseline grants no implicit
numeric-scale or timezone exclusions. Compare rejects separately with the same
complete multiset comparator after lossless typed export.

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence compare --mapping m_SFX_LOGIN_EVENT \
  --oracle parity/out/evidence/m_SFX_LOGIN_EVENT/oracle1/target.json --run1 /path/run1.json
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence replay --mapping m_SFX_LOGIN_EVENT \
  --oracle parity/out/evidence/m_SFX_LOGIN_EVENT/oracle1/target.json \
  --run1 /path/run1.json --run2 /path/run2.json
```

Outputs go under `out/evidence/<mapping>/compare.json` or `replay.json`; failures
exit nonzero. Replay requires both runs to equal oracle and each other, zero
duplicate business keys and stable generated IDs per key. Summary keys use the
actual aggregator grouping ports. Archive uses the retained event tuple because
the target lacks source EVENT_ID; tuple collisions deliberately fail the gate.
An empty archive baseline does not prove nonempty sequence allocation parity.

## Content workflow equivalence and live upload smoke

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence content-check
# Bind existing Snowflake secret references at execution time, never via files.
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence live-preflight
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence live
```

`content-check` runs the canonical full content workflow plus standalone
TEAM_MEMBER in a fresh throwaway local database and compares only the three
owned target multisets against the frozen standalone-session oracle. Nothing
from that extra workflow is uploaded. `content_workflow_equivalence.json` retains
results and local log paths. Routing notes in the manifest and per-asset files
explain eight filtered TIMEOUT logins and three rejected INFO security alerts.

Live preflight asserts 20 distinct control keys with exactly 8/12 owners, then
reads the five relevant PC_SRC landing tables and compares every row against
frozen inputs using shared-loader STG types. Internal audit dependencies remain
the frozen oracle tables, not additional landing inputs. PC_SRC timestamps use
bootstrap precision (0); baseline upload follows `commands.before` TIMESTAMP(9).
DESCRIBE verifies warehouse types before mapping exact representations into the
local snapshot metadata. Integer NUMBER(38,0) and typed PostgreSQL integers share
an exact integer representation; strings, decimal scales and timezone are not
trimmed or discarded. All query SQL, QIDs and results are retained under
`out/evidence/live`, with `transcript.txt` for human review.

`live` lists existing PC_BEFORE tables, replaces only eight owned targets,
uploads nonempty reject outputs into owned `__REJECTS` tables and checks full
readback fidelity. It uses only PC_BEFORE.CAPTURE_STAGE and the owned baselines.
It creates PC_EVIDENCE_SMOKE (fails if already present), tests identical copies
and separate duplicate/value/ID mutations, and drops its scratch schema in a
finally block. This is **HARNESS SMOKE — not mapping parity**; SECURITY_ALERT's
ID mutation tests identity stability, not a claim that ALERT_ID is generated.
Pre/post control snapshots must remain byte-identical, including on failures.

No metrics or success marking is performed. UNT-10 owns acceptance/marking with
owner `migrations-page`. Live mapping parity, DAG execution, CI/SonarQube and
final branch delivery are not certified by this harness smoke.

# Additive migration harness

Run `make sfx-pc-setup`, `make sfx-pc-licence`, and
`make sfx-pc-test` from the repository root using the shared warehouse venv.
Live commands require injected Snowflake credentials and enforce SFX_D1110_AFTER.
Setup loads only the 20261109 files referenced by workflow File Readers (no
headers), using staging column types from the runner fixture bootstrap, plus
its GL_ACCOUNT reference seed. LANDING_DIR or `python -m parity setup
--landing-dir PATH` overrides the fixture root. Run the module from warehouse/.
Setup truncates/reloads only PC_SRC tables; it does not execute mappings.

Workflow and mapping XML exports are parsed with `defusedxml`: entity
declarations and external entity references are rejected before inventory or
landing-file discovery. An ordinary PowerCenter `DOCTYPE` remains supported
without retrieving its DTD.

Workers own `mappings/sfx_billing.yml`, `sfx_content.yml`, `sfx_audit.yml`.
The YAML is a dictionary keyed by exact mapping name, with optional fields:
`key_columns` (list), `exclude_columns` (column-to-explicit-reason dictionary),
`dbt_model`, `after_table`, `before_table`, `session`, `workflow`, `patterns` (list).
Unknown mappings/fields fail validation. Exclusions are printed during setup.
Default before relations are PC_BEFORE.<target>; default after relations are
PC_<area>.<target>. STG targets have no primary key in XML or bootstrap, so their
default key list is empty: workers must explicitly choose an appropriate key.

SFX_D1110_AFTER.MIGRATION_CONTROL.MAPPINGS is seeded with a guarded MERGE: existing rows are never
changed except to fill NULL OWNER_EFFORT. Ownership assignments live in
harness.py (owner_effort / ACT3_CONTENT); 12 belong to act3-workflow and eight
to migrations-page. require_owner is the reusable write-path ownership guard.
The counter counts AMBER as still requiring PowerCenter and reports per owner.

`PC_CONTROL_SCHEMA` (or `--control-schema`) selects the existing control schema,
default MIGRATION_CONTROL. `PC_CONTROL_TABLE` (or `--control-table`) selects the
table, default MAPPINGS. These defaults also apply through Make. Setup never
creates, alters or comments the control schema or touches other objects in it;
it only creates the table if absent and adds OWNER_EFFORT if absent before
seeding. Setup loads PC_SRC first, then seeds control. Use `setup --skip-control`
to load sources without control-table access.

From warehouse/, use `python -m parity before|parity|idempotence|mark --mapping
m_SFX_PAYMENT`. `before` requires `make sfx-informatica-up`; it creates a fresh
local fixture database from bootstrap.sql, runs the full folder workflow to
populate staging/lookups, captures the target, then drops that isolated database.
It uses fresh sequence state under gitignored out/. The disabled TEAM_MEMBER
session is run explicitly after its folder workflow. NS defaults to
sfx-d1110-before; TD_PORT overrides the namespace-derived fixture port.

`parity` prints exclusions and compares normalised rows fetched on the parity
warehouse; keys without declared PK fall back to whole-row hash multisets.
This implementation fetches tables in memory; it is intended for fixture-sized
comparisons, not large-scale data volumes. Missing AFTER is a nonzero failure.
`idempotence` requires business keys (provide YAML keys for staging), builds
the selected model twice, and records row counts and excess duplicate-key rows.
`mark` reads gitignored JSON evidence, verifies configuration has not changed,
and guards ownership both before and inside the MERGE update. Default owner is
act3-workflow; --amber supplies a reason, --pr-url supplies provenance.
Idempotence refreshes parity after the second build. Capturing a new
BEFORE or running parity again invalidates the earlier duplicate-count evidence.

## Worker loop and ownership

```sh
make sfx-pc-setup                         # SKIP_CONTROL=1 if awaiting grants
make sfx-informatica-up NS=sfx-d1110-before
make sfx-pc-before MAPPING=m_SFX_PAYMENT
make sfx-pc-dbt MAPPING=m_SFX_PAYMENT      # or FOLDER=billing
make sfx-pc-parity MAPPING=m_SFX_PAYMENT
make sfx-pc-idempotence MAPPING=m_SFX_PAYMENT
make sfx-pc-mark MAPPING=m_SFX_PAYMENT OWNER=act3-workflow PR_URL=https://example.invalid/pr/1
make sfx-pc-licence
make sfx-pc-dag FOLDER=billing            # deploy suspended; RUN_ONCE=1 executes once
```

Workers own only their `warehouse/dbt/models/pc/<billing|content|audit>/`
models, `warehouse/parity/mappings/sfx_<folder>.yml`, and
`warehouse/snowflake/pc_dag/<folder>.yml`. No shared project configuration edits
are needed. The active branch has billing/content workers; audit scaffolding
is available but its control rows belong to migrations-page. Model names
`pc_billing__payment` resolve to exactly `PC_BILLING.PAYMENT` (analogous for
content/audit). Post-hooks set the required comment; a final on-run-end hook
reapplies it after adapter persist_docs and governance hooks, including for
table/view/incremental materializations.

Example `warehouse/parity/mappings/sfx_billing.yml`:

```yaml
m_SFX_PAYMENT:
  key_columns: [PAYMENT_ID]
  exclude_columns:
    METHOD_CD: "Approved normalization difference; tracked separately."
  dbt_model: pc_billing__payment
  after_table: PC_BILLING.PAYMENT
  before_table: PC_BEFORE.PAYMENT
  session: s_m_SFX_PAYMENT
  workflow: wf_SFX_BILLING_DAILY
  patterns: [Source Qualifier, Expression, Filter, Update Strategy]
```

Example `warehouse/snowflake/pc_dag/billing.yml` (SQL bodies are trusted worker
SQL; created objects in those bodies must carry the required run-token comment):

```yaml
root: START
tasks:
  START:
    sql: SELECT 1
  PAYMENT:
    after: [START]
    warehouse: SFX_D1110_TRANSFORM_WH  # optional; no other warehouse accepted
    sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SFX_D1110_AFTER.PC_BILLING.PAYMENT
  FINISH:
    after: [PAYMENT]
    sql: SELECT 1
```

Task keys must be uppercase identifiers. The helper generates
`SFX_D1110_PC_BILLING_<KEY>` in `PC_BILLING`, validates one root and acyclic
dependencies, deploys suspended, and always suspends/verifies after run-once,
including failures. No worker folder DAG YAML is shipped by the harness.
`make sfx-pc-mark ... AMBER="One-sentence reason."` records an explicit exception;
AMBER remains counted as requiring PowerCenter.

# UNT-5 security-alert evidence

This is implementation and offline/oracle evidence, **not live Snowflake parity**.
Live commands require explicit coordination. Writes are restricted to the selected
`PC_AUDIT.SECURITY_ALERT` model or newly created `PC_AUDIT_UNT5_FIXTURE` objects.
No command publishes control status or grants privileges.

## Contract

`pc_audit_security_alert` is shared by production, both isolated fixture models,
and the read-only reject analysis. Both SQ/input and expression output string
precisions are 12; trimming is ASCII space only. Critical OPEN becomes ESCALATED.
DEFAULT (including NULL severity) rejects with rowtype 3. Routed NULL keys reject
with rowtype 0 after the runner's failed update/insert. Reject values are unpadded.

PostgreSQL CHAR(12) readback includes trailing spaces. `evidence.snapshot` uses
`evidence.cell`, which preserves strings verbatim, unlike the generic
`compare.normal` string stripping. The model therefore pads non-NULL output
severity/status to 12 and comparisons use `full_compare`; no whitespace
normalization is used to hide differences. NULL and empty remain distinct.

Critical writer finishes before standard writer. A key in both routes gets the
STANDARD value. Within-route duplicate non-NULL keys have no preserved input order
in PC_SRC: the merge source calculates route-key counts and a global maximum,
then divides by zero if any count exceeds one, before its cross-route QUALIFY.
This fails the atomic MERGE (or initial CTAS), not a post-write dbt test. The
duplicate fixture is an intentional difference: runner performs both ordered
updates, whereas dbt must error and preserve its seeded initial target.
The Snowflake runtime guard still needs live execution proof in step B.

Fixtures cover all routes, mixed case/spaces, NULL key in all three routes,
NULL status/actor/document/timestamp, long severity, critical/standard collision,
seed updates, rejected seed preservation, untouched seed, and new inserts.
Landing empty fields mean NULL. The expected target and reject rows are independently
checked against the real local runner by each oracle capture.

## Local captures

Start only a throwaway PostgreSQL container; pass its loopback port in `TD_PORT`.
From `warehouse`, using the warehouse venv (also contains the runner dependencies):

```sh
TD_PORT=56415 .venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt5 oracle --scenario frozen
TD_PORT=56415 .venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt5 oracle --scenario seeded
TD_PORT=56415 .venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt5 oracle --scenario dup_within_route
```

Each command uses a uniquely named local database, bootstraps and seeds it, runs
only `s_m_SFX_SECURITY_ALERT` twice without resetting target state, and drops the
database in a finally block. It stages the committed PSV at
`<runroot>/landing/audit/SECURITY_ALERT/20261109.psv`, sets `LANDING_DIR` to that
landing root, and leaves the XML/session/runner unchanged. Captures retain exact
commands, environment overrides (no credentials), hashes, initial/input/target
typed snapshots, session logs, stdout/stderr, raw .bad files, session results,
per-writer counts, and expected-target comparisons. Frozen input SHA is pinned.

## Coordinated live sequence (not executed in step A)

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt5 preflight
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt5 fixture-load
# For each subject: production, seeded, dup_within_route
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt5 run --subject seeded --run 1
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt5 run --subject seeded --run 2
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt5 compare --subject seeded
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt5 postflight
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt5 index
```

Preflight requires the production initial target to match the frozen oracle's
initial state (absent/empty), validates full typed PC_SRC input in both directions,
and cross-checks PC_BEFORE if present without writing it. It captures all 20 control
rows, query ID and hash. Changed implementation/HEAD or control blocks a build.
Do not rerun preflight to authorize an unexpected initial state: coordinate instead.

Fixture-load refuses an existing fixture schema, creates commented schema/tables,
seeds sources and targets from the oracle initial-state files, and checks readback.
Fixture models are enabled only by `SFX_UNT5_SECURITY_FIXTURE=1` and configure
`PC_AUDIT_UNT5_FIXTURE` inline; shared dbt project config is unchanged.

Builds capture run_results, dbt.log, adapter responses, tagged query history with
insert/update counts, SQL transcripts, targets and compiled read-only reject SQL.
Comparison checks four typed full multisets, key multiplicities, raw .bad line
multisets and typed rejects, route branches, writer/merge counts, and intervening
target writes. Cross-route runner operations become one final-value dbt merge
operation. Duplicate-fixture builds must specifically fail the division guard and
leave the target unchanged. Postflight requires byte-identical control snapshots.

Output: `warehouse/parity/out/evidence/unt5/` (ignored). `index` writes
`evidence_index.json` with per-artifact SHA256/commit and `bundle.tar.gz`.
Capture HEADs remain in lineage/execution files if artifacts span commits;
index's commit is the packaging HEAD. Preserve original evidence, never overwrite
captures or alter the historical UNT-2/UNT-4 lineage gates to accept a new run.

# UNT-8 — TEAM_MEMBER (depends on PR #2682)

Scope: only `SFX_D1110_AFTER.PC_CONTENT.TEAM_MEMBER` and the new
`SFX_D1110_AFTER.PC_FX_UNT8_TEAM_MEMBER` schema. This change appends one entry
to `parity/mappings/sfx_content.yml`; it does not change existing mappings,
PowerCenter exports, runner, parameters, prior fixtures, or control rows.

## Contract

The authoritative sources are
`etl/informatica/repository/SFX_CONTENT/mappings/m_SFX_TEAM_MEMBER.XML:6-57`
and `wf_SFX_CONTENT_DAILY.XML:1079-1126,1303-1306`.
The feed is UTF-8 pipe-separated, without quotes or header, with fields
TEAM_MEMBER_ID, TEAM_ID, USER_ID, ROLE_CD, JOINED_DT. The session reads
`$PMSourceFileDir/users/TEAM_MEMBER/$$LOAD_DATE.psv`; the unchanged parameter
file supplies LOAD_DATE=20261109. Empty fields are NULL in the runner; the
XML's `*` null character is not implemented by the emulator.

The source ports truncate to 20/20/20/12/10 characters before expressions.
Three TO_BIGINT expressions accept Python-strip whitespace, signed decimal
digit prefixes, optional fractions truncated toward zero, and trailing junk.
No numeric prefix drops the row; NULL propagates. ROLE_CD is trimmed of ASCII
spaces only, uppercased, then truncated to 12 characters. JOINED_DT uses a
full-match YYYY-MM-DD expression (one or two month/day digits allowed), with
calendar validation. Transformation errors drop rows, not `.bad` records.
Writer rejects are NULL keys, any of the three integers outside signed bigint,
and PostgreSQL's unsupported NUL character in the final ROLE_CD. Rejected
updates leave existing values unchanged. The target's other columns are nullable.
Non-key overflow/NUL binding can reject the UPDATE statement even for an absent
key (UPDATE `.bad` row type 1); null/out-of-range keys with valid non-key fields
reach failed fallback INSERT (row type 0). Raw reject comparison preserves that
distinction. Initial CHAR(12) seeds are padded exactly as PostgreSQL stores them.

The session treats rows as Update, enables Update else Insert, and explicitly
disables truncation. There is no delete path. Stop on errors=0 means expression
errors do not fail the session. Writer errors are row-local. Bad rows are written
to `$PMBadFileDir/team_member1.bad`; the runner removes an empty reject file.

The model follows UNT-6's incremental MERGE materialization, not UNT-7's table
replacement. TEAM_MEMBER_ID is the unique merge key; full_refresh=false prevents
replacement through full refresh. Matched candidates update; unmatched insert;
unmentioned rows survive. The unchanged second run must preserve row values and
the target object. Initial production creation is permitted only after absent-target
preflight. Fixture targets are pre-created and seeded before either merge.

PC_SRC.TEAM_MEMBER has exactly the five staging columns and no ordinal. Ordered
last-successful-row-wins cannot be recovered from it. Duplicate accepted keys
therefore trigger a division-by-zero guard in the source query before MERGE can
apply changes. The separate dup_key fixture is explicitly **NOT PARITY**: the
oracle applies SECOND while dbt must fail atomically and preserve the initial table.

## Unicode and whitespace

Python's `str.strip()` covers 29 code points (including U+001C–U+001F, U+0085,
NBSP and Unicode separator spaces), not merely ASCII or an assumed Snowflake
POSIX whitespace class. The generated `unt8_python_unicode.sql` enumerates that
set, normalizes all Python Unicode decimal digits before prefix/date parsing,
and applies Python's complete per-character uppercase mapping, including
expansions such as ß→SS. ROLE trim remains ASCII-space-only.

`parity/fixtures/unt8/generate_unicode.py` reproducibly generates that macro
using Python's Unicode database (14.0.0 in this environment). No live UDF,
package installation in Snowflake, or unrelated object is required. The
collector records hashes of both generator and generated output, all dbt/parity/
Snowflake implementation files, and Informatica inputs for every execution.
Offline SQL parsing cannot certify Snowflake higher-order TRANSFORM/lambda,
JSON Unicode decoding, regex or date execution. Those remain live-parity gates,
not claims of runtime certification. A different Python Unicode database requires
explicit regeneration and review, not silently substituting Snowflake UPPER.

## Oracle and fixtures

The canonical task remains disabled. `startworkflow` skips it, but the direct
`startsession` path does not check task-instance enabled status:

```text
python -m runner startsession -f SFX_CONTENT -w wf_SFX_CONTENT_DAILY s_m_SFX_TEAM_MEMBER
```

`evidence_unt8 oracle` creates a uniquely named unt8_* PostgreSQL database on an
isolated local PostgreSQL endpoint, bootstraps it, stages only TEAM_MEMBER input,
seeds its initial target, and runs that exact session twice without resetting
the target or input. It captures typed targets, session logs/results, writer
statistics and raw `.bad` rows, compares against the runner-derived route
contract, proves replay equality, and drops only that uniquely named database.

The seeded fixture exercises updates/inserts/survival, nulls, overflow in all
three numeric fields, malformed numbers/dates, numeric suffixes/fractions/signs,
input truncation, ASCII/non-ASCII whitespace/digits, and é/ß/CJK role values.
Accepted keys are unique. A rejected update follows the valid update of 101;
999 must survive without input. The negative duplicate fixture has the same
typed initial rows in oracle and Snowflake.

Example local-only setup (no shared database reuse):

```bash
docker run -d --name sfx-unt8-postgres -e POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust \
  -p 127.0.0.1:55488:5432 postgres:16
cd warehouse
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt8 oracle --subject production
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt8 oracle --subject seeded
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt8 oracle --subject dup_key
.venv/bin/python -m pytest parity/tests -q
```

Every collector entry point refuses a dirty git tree. Commit implementation
before collecting evidence; evidence outputs are ignored under parity/out/evidence/unt8.
Fresh captures never overwrite existing evidence. Archive an earlier capture
before deliberately collecting a new one. UNT8_PG_PORT can select another
isolated loopback PostgreSQL endpoint; default is 55488.

```bash

SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE=SFX_D1110_AFTER DBT_ENV_SECRET_SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY=offline-placeholder \
DBT_SEND_ANONYMOUS_USAGE_STATS=false SFX_QUERY_TAG='{"run":"sfx-d1110","mapping":"m_SFX_TEAM_MEMBER"}' \
.venv/bin/dbt parse --project-dir dbt --profiles-dir dbt --no-partial-parse
# Repeat with SFX_UNT8_TEAM_FIXTURE=1; unset it for the first parse.
```

## Live commands (NOT run during offline implementation)

After explicit approval and provisioned credentials, from warehouse:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt8 preflight
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt8 fixture-load

.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt8 run --subject production --run 1
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt8 run --subject production --run 2
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt8 compare --subject production
.venv/bin/python -m parity.evidence_unt8 postflight
```

Each build launches exactly
`[python, warehouse/snowflake/run_dbt.py, build, --select, <single model>,
--step, <subject/run step>, --mapping, m_SFX_TEAM_MEMBER]`.
Selections are pc_content__team_member, pc_content__unt8_fixture_seeded,
pc_content__unt8_fixture_dup_key. No full-refresh, global build/setup, reset,
truncate, mark or control write is run. Fixture models require
SFX_UNT8_TEAM_FIXTURE=1 and write only to PC_FX_UNT8_TEAM_MEMBER.
Reject compilation selects only unt8_team_member_rejects with unt8_subject.

Preflight requires the target and fixture schema absent, checks full typed
frozen input against PC_SRC.TEAM_MEMBER, and records PC_BEFORE existence and
contents read-only. Fixture creation is restricted to the new schema, with
typed input/seed readbacks. Builds check unchanged input/control/protected
snapshots first. Compare uses typed bidirectional multisets, key multiplicities,
classification counts and typed/raw writer rejects. Duplicate preservation is
verified separately and must not be presented as target-value parity.

table and every prior PC_FX_* or *FIXTURE* schema, excluding only its own new

alongside the full sorted typed snapshots and SHA256; absent required targets

History is current-user only, not an account-wide or other-user writer audit.

class InventoryCursor:
    def __init__(self, denied=False):
        self.calls = []
        self.denied = denied
        self.deleted = set()

    def execute(self, sql):
        self.calls.append(sql)
        if sql.startswith("DROP "):
            self.deleted.add(tuple(re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', sql)))
        if sql.startswith(("DROP ", "ALTER ")):
            self.description = []
            self.rows = []
            return
        if sql == "SHOW USERS" and self.denied:
            raise ProgrammingError(msg="insufficient privileges", errno=3001)
        data = []
        if sql.startswith("SHOW DATABASES"):
            data = [("SFX_D1110_AFTER", ""), ("SFX_D1110_TEMP", "sfx-d1110"),
                    ("OTHER", "unrelated")]
        elif sql.startswith("SHOW SCHEMAS"):
            data = [("INFORMATION_SCHEMA", ""), ("RAW_BILLING", "sfx-d1110 raw"),
                    ("KEEP", "unrelated")]
        elif sql.startswith("SHOW TASKS"):
            data = [("LOAD_TASK", "sfx-d1110 task")]
        elif sql.startswith("SHOW STAGES"):
            data = [("LANDING_STAGE", "sfx-d1110 stage")]
        elif sql == "SHOW WAREHOUSES":
            data = [("SFX_D1110_LOAD_WH", ""), ("OTHER_WH", "")]
        elif sql == "SHOW ROLES":
            data = [("SFX_D1110_ROLE", ""), ("SFX_D1110_ANALYST", "sfx-d1110 role")]
        elif sql == "SHOW USERS":
            data = [("SFX_D1110_SVC", "")]
        elif sql == "SHOW RESOURCE MONITORS":
            data = [("SFX_D1110_RM", "")]
        self.description = [("name",), ("comment",)]
        scope = tuple(re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', sql))
        if any(scope[:len(key)] == key for key in self.deleted):
            data = []
        self.rows = [row for row in data if (*scope, row[0]) not in self.deleted]

    def fetchall(self):
        return self.rows


def test_teardown_dry_run_and_scope(capsys):
    cur = InventoryCursor()
    assert teardown.cleanup(cur, "sfx-d1110", dry_run=True) == 1
    assert all(sql.startswith("SHOW ") for sql in cur.calls)
    assert "Dry-run summary:" in capsys.readouterr().out
    objects, _ = teardown.discover(cur, "sfx-d1110")
    commands = teardown.plan(objects)
    assert not any('DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "SFX_D1110_AFTER"' in sql for sql in commands)
    assert not any('"OTHER' in sql for sql in commands)
    assert not any(sql.startswith("DROP SCHEMA") and '"KEEP"' in sql for sql in commands)
    first_drop = next(i for i, sql in enumerate(commands) if sql.startswith("DROP"))
    assert all(sql.startswith("ALTER") for sql in commands[:first_drop])
    assert any('DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "SFX_D1110_TEMP"' in sql for sql in commands)
    assert any('DROP ROLE IF EXISTS "SFX_D1110_ANALYST"' in sql for sql in commands)
